front: Define HFrEF, HFmrEF, HFpEF, HFimpEF by LVEF.
back: HFrEF: LVEF ≤ 40%. HFmrEF: 41–49%. HFpEF: ≥ 50% (with elevated filling pressures). HFimpEF: baseline < 40%, now > 40% on therapy.

front: List four echo criteria that support elevated LV filling pressure in suspected HFpEF.
back: 1) LAVI > 34 mL/m². 2) Average E/e′ > 14 (or septal > 15). 3) Septal e′ < 7 or lateral e′ < 10 cm/s. 4) TR peak velocity > 2.8 m/s (elevated PASP). Also estimated PASP > 35 mmHg.

front: What imaging finding on echo strongly suggests cardiac amyloidosis in a patient with HFpEF?
back: Apical-sparing GLS pattern ('cherry-on-top' bull's-eye) in a patient with concentric LVH. Also look for voltage-mass mismatch on ECG, biatrial enlargement, thickened valves, and small pericardial effusion.

front: What GLS threshold is prognostic in heart failure?
back: A GLS less negative than −14% (i.e., worse than −14%) predicts worse outcomes in HFrEF and HFpEF.

front: What quantitative echo change defines 'reverse remodeling' after HF therapy or CRT?
back: Reduction in LV end-systolic volume ≥ 15% at 6 months.

front: What confirmatory tests distinguish ATTR from AL cardiac amyloid?
back: Serum/urine immunofixation + free light chain assay to exclude AL. If negative, technetium-99m pyrophosphate (PYP) scan with grade 2–3 uptake diagnoses ATTR without biopsy.

front: Which valvular pathology is a common contributor to acute decompensation in HFrEF?
back: Functional (secondary) mitral regurgitation — from LV dilation and papillary muscle displacement causing leaflet tethering.
